cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Approve the Harmless Version
cards.instruction: Get approval for a harmless version of your plan, then gradually reveal what that approval now commits them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can I put an extra chair in the hall, beside the one you put out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Mine's out there because the paint's wet. Don't sit on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, reserved seating. Mine will be for the chair of our new tenants' committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't a committee. I only said you could leave a chair there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep that permission on the table while we choose the committee. You'll need to stay and represent the chair's owner.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies extra seating as institutional setup; A3 covers wet paint as reserved seating and reveals committee purpose; A5 claims further role obligations but chair ownership becomes ambiguous.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 furniture permission enables A3 committee claim; B4 no-committee correction enables founding meeting in A5.

relationship.evidence: B4 limits a practical permission and does not accept institutional authority.

heightening.evidence: A5 grows approval into committee selection, but why B represents which chair owner is unclear.

specificity.evidence: A1 two chairs with different owners and A3 chair/person pun overload A5 ownership reference.
